sections.h2: Where is Ottumwa, Iowa, and what does its name mean?
sections.html:
Ottumwa is the county seat of Wapello County in southeastern Iowa, at about 650 feet of elevation, and the Des Moines River divides the city into northern and southern halves. The name comes from a Meskwaki (Fox) word usually rendered as "tumbling waters," which refers to the Appanoose Rapids on the river.

The town grew on former camps of the Meskwaki chiefs Wapello and Appanoose, and it was first called Appanoose Rapids. In May 1843 the Appanoose Rapids Company claimed 467 acres. Ottumwa was named county seat in 1844, the flood of 1851 damaged it badly, and the Burlington and Missouri River Railroad arrived in September 1859.

A ferry once linked the two banks, and a bridge replaced it by 1875. South Ottumwa was annexed in the 1880s. The river still separates the north and south sides.

sections.h2: How did coal and meatpacking shape Ottumwa?
sections.html:
Coal mining began near Ottumwa by 1857, and by 1889 the state mine inspector listed 15 shafts within the city. Northeastern Wapello County has large coal and clay deposits that helped drive the early industrial growth, and the Coal Palace exhibition center was built from 1890 to 1892.

Meatpacking and farm equipment took over as anchors. The John Morrell and Company plant was a major employer from 1877 to 1973, and today JBS and John Deere still appear on the employer list. The city's population peaked at 33,871 in 1960, fell to 24,998 by 2000 and was 25,529 in the 2020 census.

A city that has shrunk by a quarter from its peak has a different housing market than a growing one, and the median value below sits near $106,300.

sections.h2: What are the key Ottumwa housing figures?
sections.html:
Ottumwa's median owner-occupied home value is $106,300, and about 61.7 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The Census Bureau estimates the city had 25,319 residents on July 1, 2025.

Ottumwa had 10,098 households in the 2020 census, and the 2020 racial and ethnic mix included 15.7 percent Hispanic or Latino residents. The median age was 36.7.

JBS Live Pork is the largest, with 2,550 jobs in the city's 2023 financial report. The Ottumwa Community School District follows at 800, and Ottumwa Regional Health Center at 692.

sections.h2: Which Ottumwa schools and colleges might buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The Ottumwa Community School District serves the city and rural Wapello County. Ottumwa High School and Evans Junior High are the upper schools, Douma and Liberty are south-side elementaries, and James, Horace Mann, Wilson, Eisenhower and Fahrney are on the north side.

Indian Hills Community College, a two-year school, occupies the former Ottumwa Heights College campus, which operated from 1928 to 1980 and merged with Indian Hills in 1979. Buena Vista University also has a regional campus in the city. The district lists its elementary schools by north and south side, so check the attendance zone for your address before you describe it to a buyer.

sections.h2: What roads, rail and transit serve Ottumwa?
sections.html:
U.S. Route 34 and Iowa Highway 149 serve the town, and U.S. 63 now bypasses it. Amtrak's California Zephyr stops in Ottumwa daily in each direction between Chicago and Emeryville, California, and BNSF runs a double-track Chicago to Omaha corridor through town with a crew change point.

  • Ottumwa Transit Authority: five weekday routes and two Saturday routes, with no Sunday service
  • Ottumwa Regional Airport: a city-owned general aviation airport
  • Jefferson Street Viaduct over the Des Moines River: on the National Register of Historic Places

Because the river splits the city, a seller can mention which side the house is on and how it connects to the highways.

sections.h2: What is Ottumwa's weather, and what does it mean for a house?
sections.html:
Ottumwa has a hot-summer humid continental climate: the average January high is 32.0 degrees and the July high is 85.7. Annual precipitation averages 36.97 inches and annual snowfall 23.6 inches, with a record high of 106 degrees and a record low of minus 27.

The flood of 1851 damaged the town severely, and the Des Moines River still runs through the middle of it, so drainage and basements are worth checking before a sale. An owner who can show repair receipts has a clearer story to tell a buyer.

sections.h2: What are Ottumwa's rental registration and code enforcement rules?
sections.html:
Ottumwa requires rental housing to be registered and inspected once every three years, and the city lists about 2,600 registered rental units. A rental permit starts with the Rental Permit Application, and the 2025 fee schedule is a separate PDF on the city's site.

The Building and Code Enforcement department, at 105 E. Third Street and 641-683-0650, handles nuisance complaints about tall grass and weeds, blighted properties and junk cars. A structure unfit for habitation gets a yellow placard on the front, and it is illegal to live in it until the violations are corrected. The Health Department posts a list of placarded houses.

  • Adopted codes include the 2015 International Property Maintenance Code
  • Most new construction and remodeling projects need a building permit
  • Permits and inspection requests go through the city's online portal

If a house you want to sell has a placard, a cash buyer can still purchase it as-is. Check what the city requires before anyone moves in again.

sections.h2: When are Wapello County property taxes due, and what is the transfer tax?
sections.html:
Wapello County property tax is due in two halves, September 1 and March 1, and delinquent on October 1 and April 1. The Treasurer's office is in the courthouse at 101 W. 4th Street, and mailed checks must be postmarked by the end of the month to avoid a 1.5 percent penalty.

Delinquent interest runs 1.5 percent per month. Taxes unpaid as of May 1 get a publication fee and are advertised for the annual tax sale, held in June, and redemption interest is 2 percent per month with certified funds.

The county recorder collects Iowa's transfer tax of $0.80 per $500, with the first $500 exempt, when the deed is presented. On the median value of $106,300, the illustration is $105,800 divided by $500, rounded up to 212, times $0.80, or $169.60. The county keeps 17.25 percent of the receipts, and the rest goes to the state. A declaration of value goes with the deed.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of an Ottumwa house work?
sections.html:
You contact us with the address and the house's condition, we review it, and if you accept the offer, a title company prepares the deed and payoff figures for closing. There is no lender appraisal to wait for.

That can suit an Ottumwa seller dealing with a placard, a vacant rental or an inherited house. We cannot name a price before seeing the property, and turning down the offer costs you nothing.

faqs.q: How often are Ottumwa rentals inspected?
faqs.a: Once every three years, according to the city. Ottumwa lists about 2,600 registered rental units.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Ottumwa?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate is $106,300 for owner-occupied homes, with median gross rent of $921.

faqs.q: When are Wapello County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 and March 1, becoming delinquent on October 1 and April 1. Delinquent interest is 1.5 percent per month.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ottumwa house with a yellow placard?
faqs.a: A placarded house cannot be lived in until violations are corrected, but it can usually be sold as-is to a cash buyer. Ask the city's Building and Code Enforcement department what must be done before reoccupancy.

faqs.q: Which employer is biggest in Ottumwa?
faqs.a: JBS Live Pork with 2,550 jobs, followed by the Ottumwa Community School District at 800.
Yes. The California Zephyr stops daily in each direction between Chicago and Emeryville, California.
